Shared radix-4 combinational divider with borrow-based digit selection
motivation:
The baseline reaches only 5.442 MHz, with a 199.837 ns, 156-cell worst
path crossing operand forwarding and the combinational ALU. The four
signed/unsigned division and remainder expressions in alu.sv are the
strongest candidate for this deep arithmetic path. CoreMark fitness
scales directly with Fmax when instruction latency and cycle count stay
constant. There are no earlier bench hypotheses or recorded lessons.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU datapath with one shared, fully
combinational unsigned radix-4 restoring divider. Convert operands to
unsigned magnitudes for DIV and REM, and use the original bit patterns
for DIVU and REMU. Precompute widened divisor multiples B, 2B and 3B.
Unroll 16 digit stages, consuming the dividend from its most significant
pair of bits to its least significant pair. At each stage form the
widened partial dividend P = 4*remainder + next_pair, calculate P-B,
P-2B and P-3B in parallel, and select the largest nonnegative trial to
emit quotient digit 0, 1, 2 or 3 and the corresponding new remainder.
Derive trial validity from each widened subtraction's borrow bit rather
than instantiating a separate magnitude comparator followed by another
subtraction. Use sufficient unsigned width throughout: divisor
multiples and partial dividends require 34 bits, and trial differences
require 35 bits to retain underflow. Expose quotient and remainder from
the same network; apply quotient sign from a_sign XOR b_sign and
remainder sign from a_sign only for signed operations. Explicitly
override division by zero before sign correction: quotient is all ones
and remainder is the original dividend. Preserve INT_MIN/-1 results.
This targets fewer serial quotient-selection stages and shared arithmetic
to improve timing and routing area. Keep the combinational alu interface,
pipeline registers, forwarding, bus handshakes, instruction cycle counts,
nret=1 and all RVFI behavior unchanged. Preserve the existing
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS substitutions verbatim and leave multiplication and
base integer operations unchanged. The main risk is that the three
parallel trials and their selection mux increase routing enough to
offset the shorter stage chain; vendor timing must verify the gain.

title: Partition DIV and REM across four registered arithmetic steps
motivation:
The baseline scores 12.12 at only 5.442 MHz. Its worst reported path
passes through forwarding and u_ex/u_alu, with 156 cells and 199.837 ns
arrival time. The current ALU implements signed and unsigned division
and remainder as combinational / and % expressions. Those operators
create long arithmetic chains that constrain the clock for every
instruction. There are no previous structural attempts in the target's
history and no LESSONS.md. Replacing this execution topology is a more
promising structural change than increasing instruction throughput
while retaining the same slow combinational datapath.
Source inspection shows that the timed list, matrix and state kernels
emphasize pointer operations, multiplication and CRC/bit operations;
source-level divisions occur mainly in initialization and reporting.
This makes extra DIV/REM latency a promising trade for higher Fmax.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep the existing single-issue pipeline and combinational RV32I/MUL
datapaths, but execute DIV, DIVU, REM and REMU in a separate registered
divider that performs eight radix-2 restoring steps per clock and
completes its 32 quotient bits in four clocks. Remove all / and % operators
from the ordinary ALU. Capture the forwarded operands and instruction
metadata once, then use a shared unsigned quotient/remainder engine
with at most eight serial 33-bit trial subtract/select updates per
cycle, rather than the baseline's full 32-step combinational divide.
Use separate registered magnitude preparation and final sign
correction; no cycle combines those with the quotient loop. Return a
result within six clocks after accepting operands: one magnitude
preparation clock, four quotient clocks and one correction clock.
Handle divide-by-zero and signed overflow explicitly. MUL, MULH,
MULHU and MULHSU remain unchanged. This is one divider-topology change;
retain the rest of the pipeline and avoid unrelated throughput work.

A valid division occupies EX until its result is available. Freeze
fetch/decode and prevent younger instructions from entering EX; older
instructions continue through MEM/WB. Once the previous EX/MEM entry
is accepted by MEM, replace it with an invalid entry while the divider
runs rather than repeatedly retiring it. A stalled older data-memory
request keeps its EX/MEM payload and bus outputs stable. Latch the
divider's result and all RVFI metadata until EX/MEM can accept them,
then enqueue the instruction exactly once. Capture operands only on
a single accepted start event, using existing forwarding, and preserve
held ID/EX source values when their producers drain from MEM/WB.
Register-file writes, redirects and memory enables require valid
instructions; divider backpressure must not suppress older commits
or replay a store. Reset cancels any outstanding division.

Retain the exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas for all eight M operations.
For DIV/REM, ALTOPS uses the same start/busy/completion state transitions
and latency as the real divider, substituting only the result formula.
The unmodified liveness checks allow ten clocks from a triggered
retirement to its successor. Keep the complete ready-bus retirement
gap, including divider launch and pipeline drain, within that bound
for adjacent divisions in both real and ALTOPS builds; do not use a
32-clock bit-serial engine or alter the formal configuration. The
arithmetic is checked with directed and randomized cocotb vectors,
including all RV32M exceptional cases. Preserve nret=1,
the core port set, decoder legality and all existing correctness gates.
The expected Fmax increase should outweigh extra cycles on DIV/REM;
verify that tradeoff with the unchanged stalled CoreMark and Gowin
fitness evaluation.

title: 64-entry folded-PC bimodal prediction at fetch
motivation:
The baseline has no branch prediction: every aligned taken conditional
branch and every JAL/JALR redirects in EX and discards the current fetch.
IF/ID is combinational, so a correctly predicted direct transfer can
eliminate the one-cycle recovery bubble without adding a pipeline stage.
CoreMark repeatedly executes loops and direct calls, making a small
adaptive direction predictor a promising way to increase iterations/cycle.
Profiling the canonical 2K, -O3, 10-iteration instruction stream between
its MMIO markers finds 529588 conditional branches, of which 294425 are
taken, plus 49367 direct JALs. A 64-entry table with a folded PC index
predicts about 92.2 percent of conditional branches correctly.
The measured critical path is the forwarded combinational M-extension
ALU, not branch lookup; this proposal targets throughput while keeping
predictor storage and added fetch logic small enough to preserve Fmax.

Add a 64-entry PC-indexed bimodal table of two-bit saturating counters,
initialized to weakly not taken (01). Index it with the six-bit XOR
fetch PC[7:2] ^ fetch PC[13:8], use
the counter MSB for legal conditional branches, and compute their B-type
target directly from the fetched instruction. Predict legal aligned JAL
unconditionally taken using its J-type immediate. Leave JALR predicted
sequential and resolve it in EX. This is one direct-control-flow predictor;
no BTB, global history, return stack, or instruction buffering is needed.

Because this core exposes imem_data combinationally in IF, the predicted
next PC can be installed at the same edge that accepts the instruction
into ID/EX. Add predicted_next_pc to IF/ID and ID/EX, and capture it with
exactly the same enable as the instruction. Compute prediction from raw
imem_data and PC rather than the flush-masked instruction bundle, avoiding
combinational feedback through the hazard unit. Restrict early branch
classification to opcode 0x63 with funct3 in {0,1,4,5,6,7}; JAL uses 0x6f.
Predict sequential whenever the proposed direct target is misaligned
or outside instruction memory [0x00000000, 0x00100000). The bounds gate
applies only to speculation and preserves architectural EX resolution.

In EX, retain the existing forwarding, branch comparison, JAL/JALR link
result, and trap handling. Form the architectural resolved next PC using
the existing semantics, including pc+4 on a misalignment trap. Redirect
and squash the younger fetched instruction only when this resolved PC
differs from the accepted predicted_next_pc. Both taken-to-not-taken and
not-taken-to-taken errors must recover, as must a wrong target. Keep RVFI
pc_wdata equal to the resolved architectural PC, never the prediction.

Only a valid EX instruction that advances to EX/MEM may issue recovery
or update the predictor: gate both with !stall_ex_mem. Train only legal,
non-trapping conditional branches, using their EX PC index and actual
outcome, once per execution. Counters increment/decrement with saturation;
simultaneous fetch and training read the old counter value with no bypass.
During load-use, imem-not-ready, or dmem stalls, retain the fetch PC and
never consume a speculative advance unless the instruction is accepted.
Once EX can advance, a misprediction correction overrides frontend stalls,
bubbles ID/EX, and discards the wrong-path fetch before it can have memory
or register side effects. Correct predictions must not trigger a flush.

Keep the single-channel nret=1 IO and all correctness gates unchanged.
Validate loop warmup/exit, forward branches, aliasing between table entries,
direct JAL, sequential JALR recovery, illegal branch encodings, misaligned
transfers, and wrong-path stores under independent instruction/data stalls.

Fmax times iterations/cycle; the expected gain is from fewer flush cycles.

percent acceptance threshold tolerates approximately a 2.4 percent Fmax

title: Parallel radix-4 digit selection inside the registered divider
motivation:
The current champion scores 68.17 at 30.617 MHz. Its worst Gowin path
runs from remainder_q back to remainder_q inside u_ex/u_div, with
38.355 ns arrival, 252 cells and 48 reported logic levels. The loop
computes eight serial restoring subtract/select steps per clock.
LESSONS.md shows that keeping division registered is essential:
pipelining improved fitness by 462.46 percent, while the earlier
fully combinational radix-4 attempt reached only 6.277 MHz. Optimize
the arithmetic within the champion's existing register boundaries
to raise Fmax without increasing CoreMark cycles or divider latency.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the eight serial radix-2 bit steps in each div_unit LOOP cycle
with four radix-4 digit steps. This is a local combinational datapath
optimization: keep the IDLE/PREP/LOOP/CORRECT/DONE state machine,
four LOOP clocks, magnitude preparation, sign correction and the
start/busy/done/accept interface exactly as in the champion.

During the existing PREP clock, normalize the divisor to its unsigned
magnitude B and register widened B and 3*B; obtain 2*B by wiring a
left shift of registered B. Use explicit unsigned 34-bit multiples,
including the carry bits of 3*B, so unsigned divisors with bit 31 set
are correct. Compute 3*B from the normalized magnitude during PREP,
never inside the repeated LOOP chain. For each of four unrolled
digits, form unsigned 34-bit P = {remainder, quotient[31:30]}.
Calculate 35-bit differences {1'b0,P}-{1'b0,kB} for k=1,2,3
concurrently. Derive ge1/ge2/ge3 from the inverse borrow bits;
no separate magnitude comparators are needed. Select the largest
nonnegative trial to append quotient digit 0,1,2,3 and obtain the
next remainder. Carry the updated quotient and remainder into the
next digit, consuming exactly eight dividend bits per LOOP clock.

Exploit the monotonic trial-valid flags to implement a flat one-hot
remainder mux: select0=!ge1, select1=ge1&&!ge2,
select2=ge2&&!ge3, select3=ge3. Mask P and the three trial results
with these enables and OR them, avoiding a cascaded priority mux
after the parallel subtractors. The quotient digit is
{ge2, ge3||(ge1&&!ge2)}. For B>0 the selected remainder is below B,
so retaining its low 32 bits is exact; never truncate P or divisor
multiples before the widened subtraction and borrow decision.
Keep explicit divisor-zero and INT_MIN/-1 overrides in CORRECT,
including the original dividend as remainder on divide by zero.
Signed quotient truncates toward zero; signed remainder follows
the dividend sign. Preserve all RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas and
their existing cycle-by-cycle handshake behavior.

Halving the serial arithmetic/selection decisions on the measured
critical path should improve Fmax enough to clear the 4.6 percent
champion threshold with the same iterations/cycle. The main risks
are the extra parallel subtractors and divisor fanout, or the PREP
magnitude-plus-3B path becoming critical. Require the unchanged
correctness gates and vendor Gowin timing to assess these risks;
do not add pipeline stages, modify frontend control, or optimize
verification-only RVFI logic. Preserve nret=1 and every invariant.

title: Give load/store addresses a dedicated execute adder and register
motivation:
The champion scores 112.68 at a median 47.218 MHz. Reproducing vendor
timing across all three placement options confirms that the scored
worst path traverses register-file/forwarding selection, a multiply
DSP and ALU result selection before reaching a data-memory BRAM
address input. The RTL exposes the general EX/MEM alu_result as
dmem_addr even for non-memory instructions. That couples the memory
address interface to every arithmetic result and permits sequential
mapping across the intended EX/MEM boundary. A dedicated effective
address register can remove this coupling without changing pipeline
depth, arithmetic latency, prediction or instruction throughput.

regressed; the successful five-step divider and predictor should stay.

title: Retimed M-extension execution with registered multiply and seeded divide
motivation:
The champion scores 112.68 iterations/second at median 47.218 MHz and
4190281 CoreMark marker cycles. The recorded structural experiments
established the value of registered division, while preserving operand
flops and separating squash control alone did not improve fitness.
A fresh, unchanged Gowin placement-option-0 run reproduces 45.508 MHz:
the worst path is 27.269 ns from WB destination selection through
operand forwarding, the combinational multiplier DSP and its result
mux to the data-memory address. The next four paths are the five-step
divider recurrence at 27.206 ns. These are effectively tied arithmetic
limits. Shortening only one leaves the other limiting the clock.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure M-extension execution as one bounded-latency registered
execution island owning EX, instead of leaving multiplication in the
single-cycle ALU alongside a separate iterative divider. The single
structural angle is to repartition both critical M arithmetic cones
across explicit register boundaries. Keep ordinary RV32I execution,
the current predictor, bus interfaces, nret=1 and retirement ordering.

Dispatch only valid legal MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU/DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU
instructions to this island. A single start captures forwarded operands,
the operation and full retirement metadata. Hold ID/EX until completion
can enter EX/MEM; let older MEM/WB instructions drain. Give the island
one busy/done/accept lifecycle and retain its completed result while an
older data-memory request is stalled. Remove all multiply hardware from
the ordinary ALU so the previous DSP-to-wide-ALU-mux path disappears.

Implement multiplication with four parallel DSP-sized limb products
captured into registers on the launch edge, followed by a registered
product reduction. Split each source into an unsigned low 16-bit limb
and a signed 17-bit high limb. The high limb is {signed_operand &&
source[31], source[31:16]}; signed_operand is true for both sources on
MULH, only source A on MULHSU, and neither on MUL/MULHU. Explicitly
widen low limbs with a zero sign bit when multiplying mixed limbs.
Register the four exact products with sufficient widths and signedness,
then reconstruct the full product with correctly sign-extended shifted
terms. Use a balanced or column-wise carry reduction, rather than a
serial chain of full-width additions. Register the assembled product
before selecting its low or high 32-bit half for EX/MEM. Launch is
followed by one reduction edge and one EX/MEM acceptance edge: two
additional EX clocks relative to ordinary ALU instructions. No extra
input-capture clock or additional sign-correction clock is permitted.
These DSP-output registers and the product register must be real timed
storage, with vendor preservation attributes if needed to stop register
absorption from rebuilding the original unregistered arithmetic cone.

Repartition the divider to consume the first four dividend bits on
launch and perform the remaining 28 bits in seven registered groups of
four restoring steps. Preserve the current magnitude capture, exact
signed correction, zero-divisor and INT_MIN/-1 overrides. Seed the
partial remainder and quotient from magnitude_dividend[31:28] divided
by magnitude_divisor. This is a four-bit numerator, not a second
general 32-bit divider: if divisor >= 16, the initial quotient nibble
is zero and the remainder is the numerator; for divisors 1..15 use a
small four-step widened subtract/select seed network or constant case
logic. Divisor zero may use arbitrary deterministic recurrence state
because the explicit architectural exception overrides the result.
Load the 32-bit quotient shift state as {magnitude_dividend[27:0],
seed_quotient[3:0]} and the remainder as seed_remainder. Each of seven
LOOP clocks shifts four subsequent dividend bits through exactly the
existing restoring recurrence. The final quotient contains the seed
nibble followed by the remaining 28 quotient bits. This reduces LOOP
serial subtract/select depth from five to four without adding a clock.
Keep sign/exception correction outside LOOP on the frozen DONE result
feeding the existing EX/MEM acceptance edge.

Retain the launch plus seven LOOP edges plus acceptance schedule for
division. Adjacent ready-bus DIV/REM retirements must still be nine
clocks apart, and an unpredicted branch/JALR followed by division must
still retire within the unchanged ten-clock liveness deadline. Do not
add a new global pipeline stage or a divider completion register that
consumes this margin. Multiplication's bounded delay is shorter and
must also meet liveness for every operation transition and dependency.

Never start using a forwarded older LOAD's effective address: wait for
its data to be available before capturing dependent M operands. Preserve
held source refresh when older WB producers disappear. Once MEM accepts
an older EX/MEM entry, emit bubbles while the island owns EX; do not
replay that entry, its memory request or its retirement. On completion,
enqueue exactly once and release the frontend on the same acceptance
edge. Reset cancels outstanding work. Invalid retained instruction
payloads cannot start either arithmetic engine, block progress, train
prediction, redirect, write registers or issue memory transactions.

Preserve all eight exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS substitutions in the new
unit with the same operation-specific real-hardware lifecycle. Move
existing multiply result vectors to handshake-aware unit tests, retaining
every arithmetic expectation and adding randomized high-product coverage;
do not replace arithmetic checks with expectations of the fast ALU's
default result. Keep the unchanged formal, decoder, cosim and canonical
stalled CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds/marker-window gates.

Expected improvement is 18 percent, with medium confidence. The gain
must come from a genuine shorter M arithmetic topology, and must exceed
multiplication's additional CoreMark cycles. At unchanged marker cycles
the 4.6 percent acceptance bar requires approximately 49.39 MHz; if
cycles increase by 10 percent it requires approximately 54.33 MHz.
Measure actual cycles and all three vendor placement options. The main
risks are multiplication frequency in the matrix kernel, launch-edge
magnitude/seed delay, product-reduction delay, and another ordinary
forwarding or branch path becoming critical. No timing or correctness
gain for the proposed circuit has yet been measured.

motivation:

hypothesis.hypothesis:

Let neg_a=signed_op && a[31] and neg_b=signed_op && b[31]. Extract the
four-bit magnitude numerator N directly from forwarded raw a. If
neg_a is false, N=a[31:28]. Otherwise N=(~a[31:28]+(a[27:0]==0))
modulo 16. A reduction tree and four-bit increment implement the exact
two's-complement identity without placing a 32-bit carry chain before
the seed. Retain the existing full-width magnitude_a for the lower
28 dividend bits captured into quotient_q.

Classify magnitude_b<16 directly from raw b. For neg_b=false require
b[31:4]==0. For neg_b=true require b[31:4]==28'hfffffff AND b[3:0]!=0:
exactly -1 through -15 qualify, while -16 and larger magnitudes do not.
The seed divisor D is b[3:0] or its four-bit negation according to
neg_b. Keep full-width magnitude_b capture into divisor_q unchanged.

For D=1..7, calculate {floor(N/D),N%D} with constant Boolean truth
masks. For each divisor and each of eight output bits, embed a 16-bit
constant whose bit N is that exact quotient/remainder output bit.
Index each constant by N, gate its eight-bit result with the shared
three-bit equality D[2:0]==divisor, and combine the eight gated terms
with a balanced OR. D=0 can deterministically return quotient zero
and remainder N because the existing architectural zero-divisor
override remains authoritative. Generate constants when writing RTL;
introduce no runtime division, remainder or multiplication operators.

remainder is T[4] ? N : T[3:0]. Select this pair when D[3] is set;
otherwise use the small-divisor Boolean result. For magnitude_b>=16,
override the pair with quotient zero and remainder N. Capture exactly
quotient_q={magnitude_a[27:0],seed_quotient} and
remainder_q={28'b0,seed_remainder}. Remove all four serial seed steps.

and shared divisor decoding, rather than a 256-entry clocked case ROM.

motivation:

topology change, preserving the ordinary pipeline, predictor and

On the accepted launch edge capture raw forwarded a, b and op into
actual preserved registers. No magnitude conversion, quotient trial

Preserve this boundary against Gowin absorption or retiming. On the
next PREP edge compute unsigned magnitudes, seed the first two
quotient bits, and register unsigned divisor multiples D through 7D
at full 35-bit width. Form 2D and 4D by wiring, 3D=D+2D, 5D=D+4D,
6D=2D+4D, and 7D=8D-D, using one parallel addition/subtraction per
non-power-of-two multiple, never a chain of successive additions.
The two-bit seed numerator is magnitude_a[31:30]. Divisors >=4
produce quotient zero and that numerator as remainder; divisors
1..3 use an explicitly enumerated 16-entry constant lookup of the
low two-bit divisor and numerator. Divisor zero uses deterministic
seed state and the existing exception override. Initialize the
32-bit quotient shifter to {magnitude_a[29:0], seed_quotient[1:0]}
and remainder to the zero-extended seed remainder. Capture original
dividend and exact quotient/remainder sign and exception metadata.

Each of six LOOP edges consumes five of the remaining 30 numerator
bits. For the radix-8 digit form T={remainder,next_three_bits} as an
unsigned 35-bit number. Evaluate T-kD for k=1..7 concurrently with
a 36th borrow bit. Select the largest fitting digit 0..7 and its
matching residual using monotonic-fit-derived mutually exclusive
terms and a balanced residual mux. With fit[k]=no_borrow(T-kD),
use select[0]=!fit[1], select[k]=fit[k]&&!fit[k+1] for k=1..6,
and select[7]=fit[7]. OR the mutually exclusive masked residuals
and encode the selected digit without a serial priority chain.
Append that three-bit digit to
the quotient shifter. For the radix-4 digit form U={new_remainder,
next_two_bits}, evaluate U-D, U-2D and U-3D concurrently with correct
widening, and select digit 0..3 and residual the same way. Append the
two-bit digit. Thus each update has two dependent subtract/select
groups rather than four or five serial restoring steps. Restored
remainders fit 32 bits for every nonzero divisor, but trial operands
and all divisor multiples must retain their full widths. Detect fit

truncate large multiples. Special divisor-zero state is overridden

retirements remain nine clocks apart; unpredicted control transfer

title: LUT-RAM bimodal predictor with serialized cold initialization
motivation:
The champion's 64-entry folded-PC BHT and direct JAL predictor already
removed most direct-transfer recovery bubbles. Earlier experiments found
negligible benefit from a larger direction table, and carrying direct
successors into EX did not improve fitness. A fresh canonical 2K/-O3/

41558 bimodal direction errors and 13735 JALRs inside the MMIO markers.
Even eliminating all these residual control-flow errors would remove
too few cycles to clear the 4.6 percent bar at unchanged frequency.
The remaining predictor opportunity is its physical implementation:
resetting all 128 counter bits and conditionally enabling each indexed
update obstructs compact distributed-RAM inference and adds reset,
decode and routing load to a small FPGA.

initialization count to zero. On each non-reset edge while count[6] is

edge that writes entry 63 changes the count to 64; then hold it at 64
until reset. Predict conditional branches sequentially during these

initialization because the single RAM write port belongs to the sweep.
Direct JAL prediction remains active throughout initialization. The
sweep must run independently of fetch stalls, dmem stalls and M holds;

Reset restarts the entire sweep, including if it interrupts a sweep.

After initialization, use the exact current index PC[7:2] XOR PC[13:8]

instantiating vendor primitives that cannot run through Verilator and

title: Share logical and arithmetic right shifts through one signed barrel
motivation:

network, so a shorter ADD carry chain alone cannot fix it. The ALU
currently expresses SRL and SRA as separate variable shifts followed
by operation selection. Sharing their barrel directly targets this
ordinary datapath without adding pipeline clocks.

must have no effect. This removes separate logical/arithmetic shift
results and their late selection while preserving combinational timing
and the complete 32-bit architectural result. Do not merge SLL with
the right barrel or add bit-reversal muxes.

title: Retimed operand delivery with flop storage and decode-stage bypass selection
motivation:

marker cycles. Its worst reported path begins at the RF memory and
crosses operand delivery and EX before reaching the fetch PC. Earlier
rounds repeatedly found RF-origin ALU, address and M-launch paths.

and BHT rewiring did not improve fitness enough. Scratch experiments
in this round isolate two limits: replacing RAM storage alone leaves
WB-tag-to-bypass-to-EX timing critical; moving bypass decisions to ID
alone leaves the RF-memory-origin cone critical. One coherent
restructuring of operand delivery must address both sides of the
existing decode/execute boundary without adding an instruction clock.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rebuild operand delivery around the existing ID/EX acceptance edge:
use fixed-word flop RF storage and register the forwarding selections
one cycle ahead in decode. EX consumes registered source choices
instead of comparing live producer tags before its operand muxes.
This is a single structural repartition of register reads and bypass
control, with the existing pipeline depth and instruction schedule.

Implement x1-x31 as fixed-address generated 32-bit flop words,
arranged in four banks of eight logical entries. x0 has no storage.
Decode write bank/row into local word enables; synchronous reset
clears all architectural values. For each independent asynchronous
read port, share row/bank address decode across the data bits and
form balanced masked-OR reductions within and between banks.
Preserve both same-cycle valid nonzero WB-to-read bypasses. Do not
infer RAM or change reset semantics. Make the existing two ID/EX
operand registers explicit preserved flops, with unchanged capture,
reset, validity-only squash and held-WB-refresh transitions. Verify
that Gowin removes the two RF BSRAMs and retains operand storage.

Move dependency comparison and youngest-producer priority from EX
to decode. For each raw fetched source, compute the selector that
will be correct after the next ID/EX edge: 00 uses the captured RF
value; 01 uses the advancing current EX instruction's next EX/MEM
scalar result; 10 uses the current EX/MEM instruction's next MEM/WB
result, including loaded data. The current EX producer has priority
over current MEM, and x0 is never a producer. Capture both two-bit
selectors with the instruction, independently of flush exactly as
ordinary payload capture. Current WB collisions are already captured
through the existing write-first RF path. The full-width selected
operands and all their consumers remain in EX at the same clock.

EX must advertise the destination and actual register-write eligibility
of the token it can enqueue on this edge. For an ordinary token this
uses valid legal control with branch/jump and memory faults suppressed;
a load is protected by the unchanged load-use bubble and must not be
offered as an EX/MEM scalar-data producer. For M completion use the
captured M metadata and acceptance event. A starting or busy M token,
invalid entry, faulting instruction or stalled nonadvancing entry
cannot become a new producer. Current MEM eligibility likewise excludes
invalid, illegal and memory-fault entries. Forward scalar/M results
from EX/MEM and final ALU/load WB data from MEM/WB, never an address
as a load value.

Registered selectors need explicit maintenance while ID/EX holds.
With an older dmem stall, EX/MEM remains in place: preserve a selected
EX/MEM source. If a selected valid WB producer refreshes a held source
register, capture its data into the operand flop and clear that WB
selector to 00 before WB valid drains. A younger matching EX/MEM
producer must retain priority over that older refresh. With the
frontend held but MEM advancing, the older EX/MEM producer moves to
WB; update each held selector to 10 only for its valid nonzero matching
destination, otherwise 00 after the existing WB refresh. M operands
and retirement metadata are still captured once on start and held
through completion. Handle bubbles, flushes, reset and consecutive
holds with these actual advance events; do not retain stale stage
identities or add an EX tag-comparison fallback to the critical cone.

forwarding freshness, older-memory stability, exact-once stores,

unpredicted branch/JALR immediately before division remains within

not-taken correction with PC+4; and aligned JALR correction with the

The tested prequalifiers are precisely:
D = !dec_is_illegal && !in.predicted_taken &&
    (dec_is_branch || (dec_is_jump && !dec_is_jalr)) &&

R = !dec_is_illegal && dec_is_jalr.

A = in.valid && !reset && !stall && !m_busy in EX, the rails are
t = A && D && (in.ctrl.is_jump || branch_cond),
f = A && F && !branch_cond, and

title: Decouple fetch with a two-entry fall-through instruction queue
motivation:
The champion scores 174.65 at 76.466 MHz with 4378154 CoreMark marker
cycles. Prior structural attempts successfully partitioned arithmetic,
memory requests, operand delivery and branch recovery, but recent
timing results put writeback-to-recovery/training and the divider
recurrence close together. Optimizing just one remaining timing cone
risks exposing the other before clearing the 4.6 percent acceptance
margin. The current frontend instead leaves a structural throughput
opportunity: it freezes its fetch PC whenever decode cannot advance,
discarding ready instruction-memory cycles during load-use bubbles,
data-memory backpressure and multicycle M execution. Later instruction
stalls then produce bubbles even though those earlier cycles could
have fetched the needed instructions. No prior structural hypothesis
in this target's history has decoupled instruction supply from issue.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Introduce a two-entry, flop-based, fall-through instruction queue
between the existing predicted fetch-PC engine and decode. This is
one structural frontend decoupling change: preserve single-issue EX,
the existing predictor algorithm and arithmetic/pipeline boundaries,
while using otherwise idle fetch opportunities to hide part of the
approximately 22 percent instruction-bus backpressure.

Each queue entry contains the existing if_id_t payload: full 32-bit
PC and instruction, the prediction actually used to advance fetch,
and validity. Keep a separate fetch PC driving io_imemAddr. When
the queue is empty, expose the current bus payload directly to ID;
a ready fetch consumed by ID on that edge advances fetch without
entering storage. If decode is blocked, capture that ready payload
and advance the fetch PC anyway. With queued entries, ID sees the
oldest entry, independently of the current bus instruction/ready.
Fetch into free storage during load-use, dmem and M holds until the
queue fills. Never advance or enqueue on io_imemReady=0. Buffered
payload and its accepted prediction remain stable until consumed
or squashed; do not recompute its prediction from newer BHT state.

Use explicit valid/occupancy state and simultaneous enqueue/dequeue
transitions that conserve tokens and maintain FIFO order. Prefer
fetch-space qualification from registered occupancy alone: when
full, pause fetch for that edge even if ID pops an entry, avoiding
a new combinational EX-hold-to-fetch-space path. In the one-entry
state simultaneous dequeue/enqueue sustains one instruction per
cycle; the empty fall-through path also sustains one per cycle.
The full state may decline a bus opportunity while popping, but
must not insert an execution bubble when a queued token exists.
Two payload slots are small enough to use ordinary preserved flops
rather than an inferred RAM or a large variable-index mux.

Separate downstream consumption from physical bus availability.
Load-use checks compare the current decode-head instruction's
source fields, not io_imemData, and use head availability as their
qualification. A valid queued head can enter ID/EX while the bus
is stalled. An empty queue with an unavailable fetch injects the
existing invalid bubble while older EX/MEM/WB instructions advance.
Older dmem backpressure and M ownership still hold ID/EX and its
forwarding maintenance exactly as today, but no longer stop fetch
until the two queue slots are occupied. The existing ID-stage RF
reads and decode-registered forwarding choices are computed for
the head on its actual issue edge, never when it is prefetched.

Keep EX recovery on its current edge. Recovery has priority over
reset-independent holds and instruction-bus unavailability: squash
both buffered entries and any simultaneous incoming wrong-path
fetch, invalidate the younger ID/EX token, and set the fetch PC to
the existing full-width correction address. On the very next cycle
the empty fall-through path presents the target instruction directly
if the bus is ready. Do not add a registered fetch-only stage or an
extra redirect clock. Preserve the unchanged nine-clock adjacent-DIV
and at-most-ten-clock unpredicted-transfer-to-DIV retirement bounds
in real and ALTOPS builds. Reset clears queue occupancy and restores
the original reset PC. Wrong-path queued M operations or stores must
never launch, issue a transaction, write a register or retire.

Retain the 64-entry folded-PC two-bit counters, their reset/index/
saturation behavior, direct-JAL and bounded/aligned direct-target
prediction, sequential JALR prediction, and exact-once EX training.
Predictor lookup occurs on the physical fetch PC, while the queued
PC/prediction accompany the accepted instruction into recovery.
Earlier fetching can change which counter version a prediction sees;
that is a consequence of decoupling, not a new predictor algorithm.
Preserve all decoder legality, fault/link/RVFI semantics, held operand
refresh, M lifecycles, memory request stability, nret=1 public ports
and every contract/evaluation file.

Expect a 7 percent fitness gain with medium confidence, from fewer
marker cycles rather than assuming a clock improvement. The main
risks are insufficient idle fetch opportunities, queue-head mux delay
on decode/RF paths, occupancy control on fetch timing, and additional
discarded prefetches around JALR or branch errors. Measure the actual
stalled CoreMark cycles and all three Gowin placement options. The
required ratio is (new median Fmax / 76.466) *

margin. This proposal has no measured implementation result yet.

instruction/data stalls, load-use and mixed M dependencies, queue

ordered head consumption separately; replace those obsolete topology
expectations with an independent FIFO/prediction model, not weaker
architectural checks. Require unchanged formal gates, full-trace

predictor training logic. The same late comparison controls fetch
recovery. Earlier comparator sharing retained the scalar operand mux
before comparison, while predictor counter and recovery-PC changes
did not clear the bar. Forwarding compact comparison predicates offers
a different way to shorten this late predictor feedback path.

Keep the BHT, direct JAL prediction, one-bit accepted direction,
registered recovery predicates and same-cycle EX correction schedule.
Change the predictor's branch-verification operand topology: compare
the late WB value before selecting the branch predicate, rather than
selecting two 32-bit forwarded operands before comparing them.

Form early_a = fwd_rs1_sel == 1 ? fwd_ex_mem : in.rs1_val and
early_b = fwd_rs2_sel == 1 ? fwd_ex_mem : in.rs2_val. These select only
registered ID/EX and EX/MEM sources. Construct three parallel comparison
planes for (early_a, early_b), (early_a, fwd_mem_wb), and
(fwd_mem_wb, early_b). The fourth plane, where both operands select the
same WB value, is constant: equality true and both less-than relations
false. Each nonconstant plane produces equality, unsigned less-than
and signed less-than; share its unsigned comparison with signed sign
correction: signed_lt = signs_differ ? lhs[31] : unsigned_lt.
This keeps late WB data out of the existing wide operand mux on its
route into branch verification. Scalar ALU, JALR, memory and M-unit
operands continue to use the existing forwarding datapath.

Register the four mutually exclusive plane-selection bits at the ID/EX
boundary, alongside the existing maintained forwarding selectors.
Compute them from the selectors' NEXT values on that edge:
  mask[0] = rs1_next != 2 && rs2_next != 2;
  mask[1] = rs1_next != 2 && rs2_next == 2;
  mask[2] = rs1_next == 2 && rs2_next != 2;
  mask[3] = rs1_next == 2 && rs2_next == 2.
Preserve the encoded forwarding selectors and their existing outputs.
The new mask must track their actual post-edge values during normal
acceptance, held WB operand refresh, MEM advance and data/M holds;
never derive it only from a newly fetched instruction. Reset produces
mask 0001. Selector 3 retains the original raw-operand default behavior.
Factor the existing selector next-state computation once and reuse it
for both encoded registers and the mask. The mask is a genuine
preserved register boundary if synthesis would otherwise absorb it.

Within each plane, combine its comparison bits with the existing
decode-registered recover_eq/ne/lt/ge/ltu/geu predicates. Gate the
resulting one-bit recovery with that plane's registered mask, then
combine four mutually exclusive results with a balanced OR tree.
Preserve the present recovery qualification by validity, reset, older
memory stall and M ownership. Also select equality/unsigned_lt/signed_lt
with the same mask for architectural branch_cond and train_taken, so
training and resolved RVFI PCs agree with recovery on every branch.

traps, links and train_valid semantics unchanged. Avoid a nine-way

comparison fanout and routing.

This is one predictor-verification topology change. It adds no pipeline

title: Balanced threshold muxes for divider residual selection
motivation:
The champion scores 174.65 at 76.466 MHz with 4378154 CoreMark marker
cycles. Recent micro_opt forwarding/comparator candidates repeatedly
expose a roughly 19 ns quotient/remainder-to-remainder path inside
u_ex/u_m/u_div. Its six LOOP clocks each contain a radix-8 digit followed
by a radix-4 digit. Each round currently converts ordered trial-borrow
flags into adjacent-fit one-hot enables before selecting residual data.
Optimize that repeated selection rather than changing pipeline depth
or the successful native FPGA carry arithmetic. Earlier micro_opt
history and LESSONS.md were reviewed; no recorded attempt uses a
balanced threshold decision tree at these two residual selections.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the two divider residual masked-OR networks with balanced
binary threshold mux trees, using existing fit flags directly. Preserve
all native 36-bit trial subtractions and all registered arithmetic.
This is one combinational selection micro-optimization inside div_unit.

The seven radix-8 trials use ordered multiples D,2D,...,7D. Their fit
flags are monotonic: if kD fits, every smaller multiple also fits. Use
fit8[4] to choose the upper or lower half of the eight residuals,
fit8[6]/fit8[2] to choose a pair in that half, and fit8[7]/fit8[5]/
fit8[3]/fit8[1] for the final pair decision. Implement exactly:
  residual8 = fit8[4]
    ? (fit8[6] ? (fit8[7] ? trial8[7][34:0] : trial8[6][34:0])
               : (fit8[5] ? trial8[5][34:0] : trial8[4][34:0]))
    : (fit8[2] ? (fit8[3] ? trial8[3][34:0] : trial8[2][34:0])
               : (fit8[1] ? trial8[1][34:0] : numerator8));
For radix-4 use the analogous two-level selection:

    ? (fit4[3] ? trial4[3][34:0] : trial4[2][34:0])
    : (fit4[1] ? trial4[1][34:0] : numerator4);

for digit generation. Do not substitute a serial priority chain or
change digit encoding without fresh timing evidence.

title: Four-entry shift-register fetch queue with fall-through decode
motivation:
The champion scores 174.65 at 76.466 MHz with 4378154 CoreMark marker
cycles. Fetch stops during load-use, data-memory and M execution
holds, wasting opportunities to hide the approximately 22 percent
independent instruction-bus stalls. Prior structural r9s1 reduced
cycles to 4095164 with two queue entries, but its 72.864 MHz median
limited improvement to 1.88 percent. This supports decoupling while
motivating additional depth and a simpler fixed-head topology.
Four fixed flop slots can cover longer downstream holds without
RAM inference or a circular-head address mux. Isolated experiments
with larger divider networks lost frequency through routing growth;
buffering has the stronger measured fitness result.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Decouple physical fetch from decode using exactly four flop-based
shift-register slots, three-bit occupancy 0..4, and empty-queue
fall-through. This is one structural frontend-buffering change.
Preserve the execution pipeline, arithmetic units and predictor.

Slots contain the existing 66-bit if_id_t layout: full PC, raw
instruction, accepted prediction and validity. Declare storage as
explicit logic [65:0] slot vectors or separate named packed registers,
not an unpacked array of a struct typedef: isolated formal testing
found that Yosys misinterprets the typedef-array declaration as one
payload, while Verilator/Gowin interpret it as four. Explicit vector
storage must pass the unmodified checks; never work around this by
altering the formal configuration. Keep a separate physical fetch PC driving
io_imemAddr. Present fixed queue[0] when nonempty, otherwise the
incoming physical PC/instruction/prediction. Expose head_available
independently of flush as occupancy!=0 OR io_imemReady; head valid
additionally requires no reset, flush or EX recovery. This prevents
availability from feeding itself through hazard-driven flush logic.

Physical acceptance is io_imemReady AND occupancy<4, qualified by
no reset/recovery. Head consumption requires head_available and
no downstream hold. An incoming instruction consumed through empty
fall-through advances fetch without entering storage. Otherwise an
accepted fetch appends at occupancy minus any simultaneous queued
pop. A queued pop shifts slots 1..3 toward fixed slot zero; a
simultaneous append overrides the vacated tail. Occupancy changes
by stored_push minus queued_pop. Distinguish fall-through consumption
from storage dequeue. Use compile-time fixed slot assignments with
decoded append enables; do not infer variable-index storage, RAM
or a circular head mux. When full, decline physical fetch for that
edge even if a queued head pops, keeping fetch admission dependent
on registered occupancy alone. Head issue still proceeds. States
zero through three sustain simultaneous fetch and issue when allowed.

Advance fetch on physical acceptance during load-use, data-memory
and M holds, filling available slots. Never advance or enqueue while
io_imemReady=0. Buffered heads can issue during physical bus stalls.
RF read addresses and load-use tags come from the current queue head,
and hazard instruction availability comes from head_available.
Decode/RF reads and registered forwarding choices occur on actual
head consumption; do not prefetch operand values or forwarding tags.
Preserve existing data/M holds, held WB refresh and load-use bubbles.

EX recovery overrides all frontend holds and physical bus stalls.
On the existing recovery edge, discard all queued and incoming
wrong-path tokens, clear occupancy, invalidate younger ID/EX and
set physical fetch PC to the existing correction target. Empty
fall-through presents a ready target on the following cycle: no
extra redirect register or recovery clock. Reset restores PC zero
and empty state. Reproduce the measured prototype's synchronous
clearing of all four slot payloads on reset/recovery; shift/append
updates occur only otherwise, with occupancy determining issue.
Wrong-path stores and M operations cannot launch or issue.

Preserve the 64 folded-PC two-bit counters, reset/index/saturation,
direct-JAL guards, sequential JALR prediction and exact-once EX
training. Lookup uses physical fetch PC, but queued predictions

algorithm. Preserve target alignment faults, links, held operands,

title: Predict through load-dependent branches and verify them in MEM
motivation:
The champion scores 174.65 at 76.466 MHz and 4378154 CoreMark marker
cycles. Prior attempts established that direction accuracy alone has
only about 1.3 percent remaining cycle benefit. Carried successors,
local counter updates, alternate correction rails and comparator planes
have not displaced the champion. An isolated training-register prototype
in this investigation preserved the marker cycles and canonical CRCs
but reached only 73.345 MHz median, with divider recurrence limiting it.
The proposal therefore targets a different source of predictor value:
using a correct direction prediction while a branch operand is pending.

A fresh run of the unmodified reference ISS on the canonical 2K/-O3/
ten-iteration ELF counted 2922016 instructions and 529588 conditional
branches between the MMIO markers. Of those branches, 135320 immediately
follow a load whose destination is one of their sources. The existing
64-entry folded-PC bimodal model misses only 2190 of these branches,
approximately 1.62 percent. The current hazard unit nevertheless inserts
a load-use bubble whenever such a branch is fetched while imem is ready.
These highly predictable branches provide a throughput opportunity that
is absent from the previous direction-error-only bound.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Use the existing direction predictor to issue an aligned legal conditional
branch behind its immediately preceding load without the load-use bubble,
and defer ONLY that branch's operand verification to the existing MEM
stage. The branch follows its already accepted predicted successor at
fetch. It remains an in-order pipeline token and retires at the existing
MEM/WB boundary after its real operands and next PC have been resolved.
This is one predictor-assisted verification change, with no global stage
addition and no changes to the BHT's capacity, index, counter transitions,
reset state, direct JAL prediction or speculative address bounds.

Exempt a load-use dependency only when the fetched instruction is a
decoder-validated conditional branch with an aligned direct target and
the valid immediately older EX token is a load to a nonzero matching
source register. Require actual fetch acceptance; absent imem data still
produces the existing bubble. Capture two pending-source bits and the
expected load destination with the ID/EX branch payload. Preserve the
normal load-use interlock for every other instruction, reserved branch
encoding, misaligned direct branch, JALR and M operation. Keep older
data-memory stalls authoritative: they hold the load in MEM and branch
in EX until the load is accepted, without issuing or verifying the branch
twice. Do not add a combinational dmem-data-to-EX comparison bypass.

A marked branch traverses EX without resolving, redirecting or training
there. EX captures its ordinary forwarded fallback operands, accepted
prediction, full direct and sequential successors, registered recovery
predicates, source metadata and pending-source bits into EX/MEM. The
fallback is important if the older load traps and does not write a
register: maintain the previous architectural source value using the
existing RF/forwarding/held-WB refresh discipline. Never substitute an
effective address or invalid load value for the branch operand.

In MEM, replace a marked source with the actual immediately older load's
WB value only when that WB token is valid, writes the captured destination
and is non-trapping; otherwise retain the captured fallback. Resolve all
six RV32I branch conditions with these operands and the carried decode
recovery predicates. Set the branch's MEM/WB RVFI source values and
pc_next to the resolved architectural result, preserving its normal
retirement order and trap policy. Train the BHT from this actual outcome
exactly once. A correct prediction permits the younger EX instruction to
advance normally, saving the load-use bubble without a new retirement
stage. Non-marked branches retain their current EX verification schedule.

A MEM mismatch is an older recovery than anything currently in EX. It
redirects fetch immediately to the full architectural direct/fallthrough
successor, invalidates fetch and ID/EX, and cancels the younger EX enqueue
on that edge. Clear the younger EX/MEM valid bit and memory masks before
that instruction can drive a memory request. Suppress its EX redirect,
training, producer eligibility and M-unit launch as well as architectural
writes. An older recovery must override frontend holds and any apparent
younger load-use/M hold; do not let ex_hold prevent the squash. A younger
MUL/DIV must not start on this recovery edge. Ordinary EX recovery remains
unchanged when there is no MEM mismatch. Qualify both recovery sources
by their actual token validity and acceptance, never by raw retained
payload. Recovery must continue to override an instruction-bus stall.

Integrate correction candidates as mutually exclusive MEM and EX rails
into the existing single fetch-PC register so adding older recovery does
not insert a serial target-priority mux into every current EX-to-fetch
path. Carry stable successor values before comparisons; qualify the EX
rail with absence of an older MEM correction. Combine correction and
normal predicted-advance/hold candidates with balanced masked OR logic.
Retain immediate validity-only squash and full 32-bit correction targets.
This integration is part of the deferred-verification mechanism; avoid
unrelated RF, ALU, divider, cache or instruction-queue changes.

MEM verification and a younger ordinary EX branch can generate two
training events on one edge. Preserve chronological training with the
existing single-write BHT and a one-entry event skid register: train the
older MEM event first and retain the younger EX event. When an event is
pending, consume it before current EX training and retain a current event
if needed. A deferred branch emits no EX event on the preceding edge,
which provides a drain slot before its MEM event, so this specific
immediate-load deferral pattern needs only one queued event. Assert this
occupancy property and check all simultaneous cases; never overwrite a
pending event or replay it during stalls. Reset clears deferred validity
and pending training. Lookup observes the old table on the update edge;
the exact accepted predicted_taken bit remains the recovery reference.

The instruction trace gives an upper bound of approximately 133130 saved
clocks before random bus overlap: one removed bubble per eligible branch
less roughly one extra recovery clock per prediction error. About 22
percent imem stalls already hide some baseline load-use bubbles, so use
approximately 100000 saved marker clocks, around 2.3 percent, as the
conservative cycle target rather than claiming the full trace bound.
At 4278154 cycles the 4.6 percent acceptance bar requires median Fmax
above approximately 78.16 MHz. Removing the generic EX operand mux from
verification of these load-dependent branches makes a modest timing
gain plausible, but the unchanged divider and added recovery arbitration
are substantial risks. Expect approximately five percent fitness gain
with low confidence; measure actual cycles and all vendor placements.

Preserve nret=1, all external ports, decoder default-illegal behavior,
conditional alignment traps, canonical CRC/UART/bounds/marker checks,
ordered exact-once retirement, real and ALTOPS M behavior and every
unmodified formal gate. Verify both pending sources, load faults, x0,
youngest-writer forwarding, branch taken/not-taken recovery, reserved and
misaligned encodings, simultaneous EX/MEM corrections, wrong-path stores
and M launches, arbitrary imem/dmem stalls and reset cancellation. Do not
relax liveness or architectural assertions to accommodate this mechanism.

Exempt only accepted legal aligned conditional branches with an immediate older-load source dependency from the load-use bubble. Preserve all other interlocks and make older MEM recovery cancel younger EX work and dominate frontend/M holds.

Capture the selective deferred-verification markers with the branch payload using validated decode and aligned direct target; retain ordinary forwarding selection, held operand refresh and validity-only squash.

Add older-recovery cancellation of EX enqueue, request masks, producer eligibility, redirects, training and M launch. Keep ordinary EX execution and arithmetic unchanged.

title: Two-slot circular fetch buffer with registered recovery discard
motivation:
The champion scores 182.73 at 80.002 MHz with 4378154 timed CoreMark
cycles. r9s1 and r10s1 demonstrated six-to-eight percent cycle savings
from fall-through fetch buffering, but their queue/control timing
erased the gain. Four-slot circular storage alone also exposes late
recovery paths into occupancy and the fetch cursor. Merely retiming
fetch-PC state in r11s1 did not improve throughput. The opportunity is
one integrated structural fetch boundary: small circular storage to
hide stalls, with recovery and training feedback terminating at
narrow registers so buffering does not lengthen the late EX feedback.
A temporary two-slot prototype of this complete boundary measures
80.357 MHz median across vendor placement options 0/1/2
(79.525, 80.357, 80.357), with 6788 LUT4 and 2345 FF. With the existing
reference CoreMark ELF and both random bus stalls, it uses 4095164
marker cycles, implying 196.224 iterations/sec or a 7.38 percent gain.
Canonical CRC/UART validation, bracket markers and memory bounds pass,
as do the existing real/ALTOPS M instruction tests. Full formal and
queue-aware pipeline verification remain implementation requirements;
legacy pipeline monitors assume physical fetch equals decode.

direction. Use one-bit head/tail pointers, two-bit occupancy and

the previous queue contents inaccessible. Register the already

title: Pipeline multiply through EX/MEM and MEM/WB with a late-result interlock
motivation:

94054 MUL and ten MULHU instructions; timed matrix multiplication makes
this an opportunity to improve throughput without another fetch stage.
The existing EX/MEM and MEM/WB boundaries can hold those two arithmetic
steps while an ordinary younger instruction advances behind a multiply.
This retains the arithmetic partition that previously improved timing.

title: Parallel bounded target arithmetic for fetch prediction
motivation:
The current champion scores 193.44 iter/sec at 79.218 MHz, with
4095164 CoreMark marker-window cycles. Its reported worst path runs
from the instruction-driving LFSR through u_if to cursor_q, unlike
earlier champions whose arithmetic or execute feedback dominated.
Fetch currently selects a B/J immediate, performs a 32-bit addition,
checks the upper twelve result bits, and then selects the next PC.
Thus opcode decoding precedes target arithmetic, and carry propagation
precedes the speculative bounds decision. Earlier predictor training
rewrites did not achieve accepted gains, and direction accuracy has
little remaining headroom. Shortening the actual fetch-target path is
the most promising predictor change at this champion.

without an opcode-controlled immediate mux before either adder.
For each candidate compute the twenty-bit low target and its carry
c from {0,pc[19:0]} + {0,imm[19:0]}. Implement each addition with
two ten-bit carry-select blocks: calculate the low ten-bit sum and

Keep explicit widths, including the carry outputs. The two B/J
candidates and their bounds checks run concurrently with predecode.

sign s=imem_data[31]. Therefore the full 32-bit architectural sum

(pc[31:20]==0 and c==s),
(pc[31:20]==1 and s==1 and c==0), or
(pc[31:20]==0xfff and s==0 and c==1).

title: Balanced bytewise branch verification for the predictor
motivation:
The champion scores 209.10 iterations/second at 85.630 MHz. Direction
accuracy has little remaining cycle headroom, and the r14s2 direct-target
cache timed out in formal. Predictor recovery and training still consume
forwarded 32-bit branch comparisons; timing probes show these cones
feeding decode's forwarding maintenance and operand enables. Prior r8
work showed that sharing comparison relations can help, while r9's
replicated forwarding planes regressed. A single balanced segmented
comparator targets verification without extra speculative state or a
later recovery stage. Scratch recovery-presentation retiming probes
measured only 81.532 and 76.498 MHz and are excluded from this proposal.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the predictor's EX conditional-branch comparison topology
with four parallel unsigned byte comparisons and a balanced two-level
lexicographic merge. Retain the existing registered forwarding choices
and the same forwarded rs1/rs2 operands; do not replicate operand planes,
modify scalar ALU comparisons, or add a verification/recovery clock.

For byte k=0..3, compute eq[k] = rs1[8*k +:8]==rs2[8*k +:8] and
lt[k] = rs1[8*k +:8]<rs2[8*k +:8]. Merge bytes into two halfword relations:
pair_lt[k] = lt[2*k+1] || (eq[2*k+1] && lt[2*k]), and
pair_eq[k] = eq[2*k+1] && eq[2*k]. Then derive
unsigned_lt = pair_lt[1] || (pair_eq[1] && pair_lt[0]),
equal = pair_eq[1] && pair_eq[0], and
signed_lt = (rs1[31] XOR rs2[31]) ? rs1[31] : unsigned_lt.
Use explicit unsigned eight-bit slices. The highest differing byte
determines unsigned ordering; a sign difference alone determines signed
ordering. This bounds each local comparison chain to eight bits and
shares equality, signed and unsigned relations rather than synthesizing
separate full-width relational operators for each recovery predicate.

Use these same three relations and their inversions for both architectural
branch_cond and the existing prediction-relative recover_eq/ne/lt/ge/
ltu/geu gates. Preserve the registered decode predicates and existing
EX valid/reset/stall/M-owner qualification exactly. Keep actual resolved
next-PC, train_taken and recovery consistent for every legal branch and
every forwarding source. Preserve JAL/JALR targets, alignment faults,
links and all full-width correction values. The 64-entry folded-PC BHT,
delayed training, old-counter lookup, accepted direction bit, direct
target arithmetic and two-slot fetch queue remain exactly as today.

Preserve nret=1 and every public port, raw-payload/validity separation,
immediate wrong-path squash, data/M holds, held-WB operand refresh,
load-use behavior, memory request stability, arithmetic and retirement.
Keep all existing tests and formal gates. Add equivalence assertions
under RISCV_FORMAL for equal, unsigned_lt and signed_lt against native
full-width reference comparisons; verification-only logic is not timed.
Test equal operands, the highest differing byte at every position,
adjacent values across byte/halfword boundaries, signed extrema and
sign changes. Exercise every branch funct3 and every registered forwarding
selection, held operands, both prediction directions, simultaneous bus
stalls and wrong-path store/M suppression through the pipeline.

Require cycle-identical predictions, training, redirects, architectural
retirements and the 4095164 CoreMark marker cycles, plus all canonical
CRC/UART/bounds checks. This is a frequency hypothesis. At unchanged
cycles, acceptance needs median Gowin Fmax above approximately 89.57 MHz
and fitness above 218.7186 iterations/second. Check the actual vendor
netlist for parallel byte relations and two merge levels, and inspect
recovery/training paths rather than counting operators in RTL. Scalar
ALU or divider timing can still cap the benefit; a six percent gain is
low confidence until all three vendor placements have been measured.
